title: The Three Origins
summary: Firstborn, changelings and inanimae.

claims.text: An origin is one of the three races of fae: inanimae, changelings and firstborn.
The firstborn are true fae who rose from the Mists of Creation long ago; new ones are born to firstborn or are sprites changed by strong cantrips.
Changelings are part fae, part human: made when a firstborn infant is swapped for a human one, which yields two changelings, or when humans stay long in fae realms and learn the Dominions.

Inanimae are fae of the natural world, usually springing from a natural thing of one of the five elements (wood, water, fire, earth and air). They can breed with their own element, though most find the idea repulsive.

title: The Four Courts
summary: The seasonal factions of the fae.

claims.text: A Court is one of four seasonal factions; it shapes a fae's ideas, upbringing, magic and mien.

The Saining brings a fae into a Court in three steps: the Cleansing, three seasons living by the Court's ideals; the Naming, receiving a Courtly name; and the Acceptance, finishing training and formal entry.
Solstice fae, or Disgraced fae, never Sained, refused, were exiled, or had their Naming botched; they are scorned outcasts who find work as couriers and mercenaries.

title: The Oath-Truce
summary: The hundred-year peace between the Four Courts.

claims.text: The Oath-Truce is a pact among the Four Courts to halt hostilities for a hundred years.
It began in AD 1130 and so will end around 1230.

title: Agendas and the Patrons
summary: The political aims that cut across the Courts.

claims.text: An agenda is a fae's broad political or social aim. The common ones are Constantinian, Humanist, Militant and Truce-Bearer.
The Patrons count as an agenda but are really an organised faction, not a loose philosophy.
The Patrons want seasonal rule back: each Court ruling in its own season, then handing power on.

title: Dominions and Cantrips
summary: The four spheres of fae magic.

claims.text: A Dominion is one of four spheres of magic, each ruling a set of associations: Dawn, Day, Dusk and Night.
A cantrip is one specific magical use of a Dominion.
Unleashing lets Dominion magic loose without shaping it into a cantrip, steering it toward a hoped-for end; it is always obvious, and dangerous if it runs wild.

title: Weaving and the Mists
summary: The balance of order and chaos in fae magic.

claims.text: The Mists are the magical energy of Creation; fae use them both for magic and to hide from mortals.
Weaving is the force of order that lets fae channel Dominions into cantrips.
A fae whose Weaving grows too strong becomes Locked: unable to Unleash, and obsessed with order and routine.
A fae whose Mists grow too strong becomes Lost: unable to cast cantrips, and obsessed with chaos.

title: Mien and Features
summary: A fae's true form.

claims.text: The mien is a fae's true faerie form, in which its Features show.
Lesser Features are only for looks; Greater Features also have effects in play.

title: Sprites, Fostering and Oathcircles
summary: Other words of fae life.

claims.text: A sprite is a minor fae spirit, usually bound to serve a stronger fae; one might be a cloud of butterflies, another a small blue flame. Sprites can grow into firstborn.
Fostering is the time before the Saining when a young fae learns fae society, history and the Dominions.
Every fae learns the Fostering tongue early, but most use it only when no Courtly language will serve.
An oathcircle is a band of fae bound by a shared purpose, whether war, exploring or company.

title: Iron
summary: The metal that wounds the fae.

claims.text: Only pure, cold-wrought iron harms the fae; steel and other alloys do not, and no one knows why, though some think an oath lies behind it.
Pure iron weapons deal aggravated damage to fae in every form, which can still be soaked, and each wound costs a temporary Mists point.
Iron mixed with other metals has no special effect on the fae.

title: Echoes and the Church
summary: What drives the fae back.

claims.text: Iron and salt repel the fae for reasons none of them fully understand.
The greatest source of Echoes is the Church: many fae shrink from a cross or a church bell.

title: The War of Seasons
summary: The long war among the Four Courts.

claims.text: The Courts fought for many years, ending in the dreadful Battle of Stone in the fourth century AD.
Before that battle a fae who wished to leave the Court of upbringing for another was shamed, or killed if the Court was Winter or Summer.
The fighting went quiet only after the Courts nearly wiped one another out, and many fear it could happen again.

title: The Battle of Ice
summary: A battle fought without firstborn.

claims.text: It was fought on a field near the Crystal Fortress, where neither side could gain enough edge to take the fortress from the Winter fae.
No firstborn took the field; inanimae led squads of changelings and enslaved mortals.

title: The Battle of Stone
summary: The battle all four Courts lost.

claims.text: It came about three mortal centuries after the Battle of Ice, around the time Constantine I turned Christian.
When it ended every one of the Four Courts had lost; many posts stood empty, and changelings grew so numerous that the Courts had to treat them as equals.
One survivor's view is that it settled nothing in the war and only split the fae from the world.

title: The Spread of the Church
summary: How the faith of Christ pushed the fae aside.

claims.text: Churches and crosses spread across lands once given to worship of the fae, while most Courts were too inward-looking to notice.
Many fae strongholds fell into disuse, and people stopped coming to the faerie mounds to dance under the full moon as they once promised.

title: Heritage and Age
summary: How the fae reckon age by era.

claims.text: Before the Battle of Stone the fae did not count age at all, naming an old one by status instead.
Fae born before the Battle of Stone are of Golden Heritage; those born between that battle and the Oath-Truce are of Stone Heritage.

title: Golden and Stone Oaths
summary: Ancient oaths sworn with humanity.

claims.text: Long ago the fae learned to forge oaths with humankind at large; these are the rarest oaths a fae can hold.
Oaths from the Golden Age, sworn between fae and whole nations, are the most powerful kind, and that knowledge was lost at the Battle of Stone.
Stone Oaths come from between the Battle of Stone and the Oath-Truce and are rare, since the fae kept away from people then.
Very old self-forged oaths can be dangerous for their age, though most are narrow deals of protection, privacy or shared aid.

title: The Spring Court Today
summary: A Court tired of standing still.

claims.text: Most of the Spring Court want no more of the suspended hostilities that followed the Battle of Stone or of the Oath-Truce; both were stretches of still time it disliked.

title: The Summer Court Today
summary: A Court of conquest and guile.

claims.text: The Summer Court takes weakly held domains of other Courts in regency, without needing open force.
Well-defended holdings may find that the latest diplomats and visitors are scouts for a massed Summer attack.

title: The Blind Lord's Domain
summary: A Winter holding that is both feared and crowded.

claims.text: Prince Callicantzaroi poses as a kind ruler, but most Winter fae there know the prince means murder for many visitors, and well-trained soldiers carry out even quiet wishes.
The other Courts see it as a death trap for those who displease the blind lord, yet it is one of the busiest Winter domains in Western Europe.

title: Dominion Levels and Court Ties
summary: How strong a cantrip can be.

claims.text: Each Dominion has five levels; the higher the level, the stronger its cantrips.
A fae gets a bonus with the Dominion of the home Court: Winter with Night, Summer with Day, Spring with Dawn.
Level-one cantrips are small or brief, usually touching only the caster or one person within reach.
Some effects come at different levels by Dominion; Dusk, given to travel, can cast one travel magic at level two where others need three.

title: The Dominion of Day
summary: Light, faith and fire.

claims.text: Level-one Day cantrips allow limited mind control, calling up fire and boosting the caster's presence, but cannot force acts against a target's basic nature.
Unlike Dawn and Dusk, Day can deal small aggravated wounds at range at one level, and it can burn poison out of a body, painfully.
Unleashed Day makes the caster glow like gold with crackling hair, embodying faith, fidelity and light, and onlookers find it hard to look away.
Day drains faith, confidence, loyalty and fidelity.

title: The Dominion of Night
summary: Darkness and cold.

claims.text: Night deals with darkness and cold and is tied most closely to the Winter Court.
Gloom makes a small patch of darkness for hiding; Mindveil cannot read or rule minds but shields the user's thoughts from prying magic.
Freeze Death cannot truly heal but can stop someone from dying, holding the body as it is.
At higher levels Night can harm a group of foes with aggravated damage or shield as many as 20 allies; it drains joy, delight and elation.

title: The Dominion of Dawn
summary: Earth, growth and purity.

claims.text: Dawn at higher levels can call protection from the earth and the great forest trees.
Brew and Bread is one of its cantrips; Dawn cannot read or control minds.
Dawn drains innocence, purity and virtue.

title: The Dominion of Dusk
summary: Travel, decline and atonement.

claims.text: Dusk leans toward travel.
Few fae reach its highest level; those who do are among the most dangerous, and legends speak of drying a foe away.
Amends cannot control minds but nudges a target toward contrition and atonement.
Unleashed Dusk begins faintly and swells into an eerie, haunting melody.

title: Moving an Element
summary: A basic cantrip over a Dominion's element.

claims.text: The player rolls Dominion + Wits and needs one success; the element moves for a turn per success.
It cannot change the element's nature: fire will not eat iron and water will not freeze at once.

title: The Crystal Fortress
summary: An ice citadel older than the Golden Age.

claims.text: The ancient ice fortress lies in the far north of Scandinavia, just past the Arctic Circle.
No scholar knows who built it; it predates the Golden Age and may hold the secrets of where the fae and their magic came from.
When the sun is down, travellers must wait for the Nordlys to light its walls and make spires and arches glow.
The Summer Court has held it for a century, expecting the other Courts to come for it when the Oath-Truce ends.

title: Glastonbury
summary: A place where old ways fade.

claims.text: A reclusive fae leader seldom left Glastonbury Tor or received visitors.
Between the Battle of Stone and the Oath-Truce, the people of Glastonbury lost their ties to the old ways.

title: Verdoren
summary: A great lord of the wood.

claims.text: In the Golden Age Verdoren's court was among the most important of all, guarding human settlements near the edges of the wood.
Some hope to bring Verdoren back to battle, or at least to win over Verdoren's great army of children.

title: The Vanished Kingdom
summary: A realm that disappeared.

claims.text: After the Battle of Stone one whole kingdom vanished without trace, and no one noticed until the Oath-Truce was signed.

title: The Fae and the Werewolves
summary: Old enemies and allies.

claims.text: In the Golden Age and the War of Seasons the Courts and the werewolves fought against and alongside each other by turns, making passing alliances.

title: Faerie Treasures
summary: Crafted wonders and Golden Age relics.

claims.text: A master craftsman might weave a shawl that stirs love in everyone who sees it, yet the relics of the Golden Age far surpass such trinkets.
Some Winter treasures are cauldrons with powerful Winter firstborn oathbound inside; each must be washed in human blood after use, or the bound fae goes free. Only two have been found.
